registration.description: Vessel registration establishes legal identity, ownership, home registry, certified configuration and transponder identity.
registration.cost_model: Registration charges an initial or renewal fee based on hull class, declared configuration and inspection requirements.

states.meaning: Registration and certified configuration are valid.
A major alteration has made the recorded configuration stale; vessel may face operating restrictions until inspected.
Registration was not renewed by its required date.
Registry authority has temporarily invalidated registration due to safety, ownership or compliance issue.

major_change_examples: main engine model or thrust geometry change
reactor replacement with materially different output
minor_change_examples: interior storage changes within certified mass limits
renewal_flow: Captain submits configuration and ownership record.
Approved surveyor or registry inspector verifies required items.
Government issues updated registration and machine-verifiable certificate.

yard_behavior.behavior: Normally requires registry identity for major work and reports configuration-changing work to the vessel's registry or provides documentation for renewal.
May perform work before registration is renewed; captain remains responsible for becoming compliant before entering restrictive ports.
May perform undocumented structural or propulsion work and may not ask whether the ship is registered at all.

consequences_of_unregistered_operation: refusal of docking at some ports
possible fines where local law requires registration
registration.design_intent: Unregistered operation is a viable choice with economic and geographic consequences, not an automatic criminal-state flag.
